rationale: Both are the roadmap's one M4 milestone on the same per-adult mail agent, the same read-only Gmail grant and the same open decision (personal mail on the cloud model): G015 is the locked-down reader with the on-request lookup, F016 is the 07:00 job that runs on that reader, and G015's own caveat already names the digest as the first scheduled job that reuses it. Round 1 kept the digest apart on a record that still carried reply drafts and had no dependency list; the drafts have since been taken out and round 2 wrote in that the digest runs on G015 and waits on the same decision, so both halves are wave C, medium risk and read-only, each texts only the mailbox owner, no agent boundary is crossed, and the school mailbox (F051) and the email-to-self sender (F049) stay separate cards.
name: Each adult's own Gmail, read-only, through a locked-down mail agent: 'did I get an email about X?' on request, and a 07:00 action-items digest

rationale: Both give a parent oversight of what Happy wrote on their behalf, one by showing the list and one by reversing its last entry, and both read the same per-write journal in the household store: each record names the other for that table, and round 2 noted on CRT-01 that the two would be built in one piece of work and on G006 that it should share one journal with undo, because the rows have to be written inside each write tool to capture the before-state. Both are medium risk on the parent's own agent and limited in code to the asker's own rows, and everything CRT-01 depends on is in wave A or B (the calendar write it reverses, F010, is itself wave B), so wave C reflected ordering after G006 and not a later dependency; the card states the report-only review, the undo with its inverse writes (including a delete on the Reminders bridge limited to items Happy itself created) and the operator's forget step as separate parts.
name: Happy's own change journal: a weekly review of what it did and remembered, 'undo that' for its last write, and forgetting a conversation on request

rationale: Both are operator-only checks that tell Tony after each change whether Happy is still sound, one on health, sign-ins and audit findings and one on behaviour (no secret echo, no fake 'done', pending kept apart from done), and round 2's own note on AUT-09 says its few cases could ride on this card; AUT-09 is small, no other entry refers to it and it leaves Tony nothing separate to decide. Both are low risk and touch nothing live (the cases run only against eval clones with messaging denied), and wave B was not a real dependency, since four of the cases apply today and the rest are added as reminders (F007) and memory (F041) land in wave A, so the merged card ships in wave A and says that the eval cases cost model tokens on each run while the host checks call no model.
name: Operator self-checks: daily integration health and credential expiry, a security audit after every update and monthly, and behaviour cases in the eval suite

rationale: MKT-02's build note says it adds no tool and that the one thing built is a small operator-reviewed skill fixing the quiz format, and that skill travels through exactly the pipeline AUT-06 sets up (a skill file in the config repo, Tony's review, the deploy step, the read tool on the parent's agent) in the same wave on the same agent; round 2 noted it could be the first worked example on the routines card, which also matches the roadmap rule of skills inside an agent for everything that shares its permissions. Nothing is hidden: the card names the quiz as its first skill, keeps the parent-run rule (no child chats with a cloud model; that version waits for F072) and carries MKT-02's medium risk because the photo route sends a school worksheet to the cloud vision model under the attachments decision in F002.
name: Teach Happy a routine (operator-reviewed skills), with a parent-run practice quiz from a study-guide photo or a word list as the first skill

rationale: The Places lookup is a tool on the research agent that the planner's build note composes in every run, F028 is the only entry that depends on it, and since round 2's edit F021's own description says its main use is place data for the planner and that a one-off 'is it open now?' is quicker in the maps app on a parent's phone; the roadmap's research-and-trips milestone likewise lists the maps connection as part of the same research agent. Round 2's merge reviewers kept F021 apart for its billing decision while proposing a wider options-research card that was never made; on the card that exists both are wave C on the same memory-less agent with no booking or payment tool, and the merged card states the Google key with billing switched on and the goplaces-or-Grounding-Lite choice as its own step and carries F028's medium risk.
name: Trip and outing planner (day trip, weekend, multi-day), with Google Places data for hours, ratings and distance

rationale: Talk mode is a feature of the same App Store app on the same phone, reached through the same pairing, the same wave-A deny list (MAC-04) and the same access-level decision; after round 2's edits VOX-01 points to OCL-01 for the install, the pairing and every pairing caveat, and what it adds is the Talk settings plus realtime voice as a later option, which round 2 folded into it so no third card waits on the boundary any more. Round 2's purpose pass proposed this pairing and neither history records a verdict against it; both are wave D, high risk and Tony's phone only, and the card states three steps separately (the app with chat and tap approvals, the experimental native Talk loop, then realtime voice with raw audio going to OpenAI on its own key and budget), so the riskier steps are not hidden.
name: OpenClaw iPhone app on Tony's phone: pairing with device commands denied first, chat with files and tap approvals, then Talk mode (native speech loop first, realtime voice as a later option)

rationale: Both are the roadmap's single kids milestone ('text, then voice'): the kitchen speaker is a second way for a child to reach the same tool-less, memory-less kids agent, it lists that agent as a dependency, and its own record rules out an adult-only interim version, so it has no use apart from F072. Both are 'later' and blocked on the same local model, so neither asks Tony for anything today; the card states the text route and the speaker route as separate steps, names what only the speaker needs (the device, a Home Assistant VM and a kids-only shim so the speaker never holds an operator credential) and carries VOX-11's high risk.
name: Kids' own Happy (waits for a local model): text from their own handle first, with homework hints, chat hours, parent alerts and a nightly digest, then the Home Assistant Voice kitchen speaker

rationale: Both are what a parent types into the thread to control Happy itself, and the two records already describe themselves as two levels of one stop control (/stop ends one answer in one chat, the phrase stops everything); OCL-06 builds nothing beyond a cheat sheet and one config choice, G005 is its only dependency and no other entry refers to it. Both are wave A and low risk and neither adds a tool, a recipient or a data source; the card says which part works today (the five built-in commands) and which needs the in-house plugin (the stop and lock-out phrases), keeps Tony's choice about leaving /restart and /update reachable from chat, and leaves mute and vacation mode with the notification policy (G001, wave B).
name: Controlling Happy by text: the built-in commands (/stop, /new, /status, /usage, /tools) and the stop-everything and lock-out phrases
